Definition: apparently a prime word; properly, a story, but used in the sense of G1868; praise (of God):--praise.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and both times praise comes from the lips of the lowly. Jesus quotes Psalm 8 to the chief priests — Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise — while the children cry Hosanna in the temple; and the blind man of Jericho, his sight restored, follows Jesus glorifying God while all the people give praise.
TheologicalSignificance: I love that the word belongs to children and a blind beggar, not to the educated. God perfects praise from mouths the world would ignore, and the chief priests' anger only proves the point: true praise always threatens those who want worship on their own terms.
RelatedEvents: The Cleansing of the Temple; The Healing of Bartimaeus
